value.overview: The Black Rosy-Finch (Leucosticte atrata) is a finch recorded in the United States. Field recognition often comes from dark rosy-finch body, blackish tones, pink wing and belly highlights, and high-elevation flocking behavior. In the U.S. source data, it appeared in 9 state or DC summaries, including AZ, CO, ID, MT, NM, NV, OR, UT, WY. It is most associated with Tundra:  Alpine, and local season should be checked before trip planning.
value.classification: The Black Rosy-Finch belongs to the family Finches, Euphonias, and Allies in the order Passeriformes. This is the practical birding classification used for the BirdIntel profile cache.
value.identification: Look for dark rosy-finch body, blackish tones, pink wing and belly highlights, and high-elevation flocking behavior. Also use size, posture, flight style, voice, behavior, habitat, and season. Plumage can vary by sex, age, molt, and light, so the safest identification comes from combining several field marks rather than relying on one color or feature.
